summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Shere Bangla National Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 260/10 (78.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Australia countered with 217/10 (74.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 7-Wicket Spell: Nathan Lyon (7/82), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Shakib Hasan delivered a masterclass for Bangladesh (89 Runs & 11 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Bangladesh 55%) and allowing Bangladesh to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Australia faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Bangladesh's bowling unit, bolstered by Nathan Lyon (12 Runs & 10 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Bangladesh won by 20 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Bangladesh's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Australia produced fighting phases, Bangladesh won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
